ac5_shortfall.note: No amount of class-creation tuning affects AC5. The gate removed the generic dispatch for exactly-typed scalars and delivered ~11%; reaching 20% requires attacking the remaining per-field cost (conversion and the _dc_method_setattr_ path) or the structural costs TASK-15 rejected as unsafe.
options: further compatible optimization (new task, gate-owner scope)
a reviewed spec change to the AC5 threshold
carry the shortfall into the TASK-17..20 experiments, which are explicitly measured against this frozen candidate

assignment_and_to_dict.note: Both exceed the 0.95% cross-build floor, so they are real, but both are inside AC6's 5% median limit. assignment's p95 of +11.77% is the item that needs explaining before AC6 can be signed off.

class_creation.candidate_remediation: The abstract.py:356 call is redundant: the __new__ loop rebuilds from the final field set, which TASK-11 made authoritative precisely so cache hits and inheritance are handled. Removing the earlier call should recover ~18.4 us on an 8-field class. Additionally, build_field_policy allocates a frozenset per field even when there are no constraints, which is the bulk of its 2300 ns.
class_creation.cause: TASK-11's build_field_policy runs at class creation. Measured at 2300 ns per field, and it is invoked from TWO call sites: abstract.py:356 (_initialize_fields, per new field) and abstract.py:443 (__new__, over the FINAL column set). For an 8-field class that is ~36.8 us of the ~65 us observed regression, and roughly half of it is redundant.
class_creation.scope_note: NOT applied here: modifying production sources is explicitly out of scope for TASK-16. This is a recommendation for the gate owner (TASK-11/TASK-13 scope) or a follow-up task.

frozen_candidate.note: Frozen as the optimized-Cython comparison point for TASK-17..TASK-20, regardless of the AC5 shortfall: later experiments must beat THIS, not the 0.10.21 reference.

AC5_construction_improvement.note: Both Employee shapes fall roughly half short. Even the optimistic end of the interval is ~12%.

AC6_regression_limit.note: class_creation's point estimate (4.91%) is under 5% but its 95% interval reaches 5.72%, so <=5% cannot be claimed with confidence. assignment's p95 is 11.77%.

headline: AC5 IS NOT MET. Employee construction improved 10.6% (raw) and 11.0% (native); the specification requires 20%. AC6 is also not cleanly met: class_creation regressed 4.91% with a 95% CI upper bound of 5.72%, and the assignment p95 regressed 11.77%. Compatibility is perfect (0 divergences everywhere) and the dispatch budgets pass. This task therefore REMAINS INCOMPLETE: per its own acceptance criteria, a shortfall is not a waiver.

measurement_quality.note: The 20% AC5 target is resolvable at this noise level, so the shortfall is a real result and not a measurement limitation.

noise.guidance: spec §4: if machine noise prevents distinguishing a 5% regression, rerun in a controlled environment rather than declare success. A calibration spread above 10% means this machine was not quiet; treat every inconclusive verdict as 'measure again', not 'no change'.

noise_floor.definition: half-width of the 95% bootstrap interval on the paired median ratio, expressed as a fraction of 1.0
noise_floor.guidance: an effect smaller than the worst resolvable effect must be reported as inconclusive and re-measured in a quieter environment, never rounded into a claim

multiple_comparisons.caution: each verdict uses an independent 95% interval, so across 15 workloads roughly 0.8 spurious 'regression' or 'improvement' labels are expected per run by chance alone. A single flagged workload whose effect is near the noise floor is not evidence; look for an effect that is large relative to the resolvable effect, or that reproduces across independent runs.

raw_samples_reference: Embedded in this file under `raw.reference` and `raw.candidate`: one entry per process, each with per-batch samples for every workload. `diagnostics` holds the allocation/lifetime observations, collected in a SEPARATE pass with tracemalloc and never while a timing was in progress.
reproduce: python benchmarks/model_performance.py --pin-cpu <cpu> --control-root <second independently built worktree of d932c720> --output benchmarks/results/compatible-model-performance/cython-acceptance.json

same_source_control.conclusion: treat any movement within the empirical cross-build floor as no change, regardless of what its confidence interval says. A single workload flagged near this floor is not evidence; a real result must be large relative to it and reproduce across runs.

noise.guidance: spec §4: if machine noise prevents distinguishing a 5% regression, rerun in a controlled environment rather than declare success. A calibration spread above 10% means this machine was not quiet; treat every inconclusive verdict as 'measure again', not 'no change'.

same_source_control.purpose: calibration: both sides are the SAME commit built independently, so the true ratio is 1.0 everywhere. Anything else this reports is harness noise plus binary-layout effects.
